claim: Locating the fault is the hard part of debugging for people; fixing is easy once the location is known. Human data are old (Katz and Anderson 1987, Vessey 1985) and the 66% diagnosis-time share is second-hand.
agent_test: Compare agent with a forced locate-then-patch step against direct patching at equal tokens; log location accuracy separately from fix rate.

claim: In LLMs, finding the wrong step is much harder than fixing it when told where: best mistake-finding 52.87% (GPT-4); true location lifts originally-wrong answers by +23.5 to +43.9 points, random location by +11.8 to +21.6, and both cost -6.7 to -15.9 on correct traces. Re-checked.
agent_test: Give the agent an externally supplied location vs its own guess vs random; measure gain and damage to correct answers.

claim: Without external feedback, LLM self-revision of reasoning answers does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds). Reported gains came from oracle labels (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59). Re-checked against the paper.
agent_test: Run the revise step with and without a real checker; count right-to-wrong flips at equal tokens.

claim: Real execution output is what makes self-debugging work. With unit tests Self-Debug gains +8 to +12 points (GPT-4 MBPP 72.8 to 80.4-80.6, TransCoder 77.3 to 88.8-90.4); without execution gains shrink to about +1 to +4 and Codex MBPP simple feedback falls 61.4 to 57.6. Re-checked.
agent_test: Ablate execution results in the revise loop; compare real output vs model-imagined output at equal tokens.

claim: Showing runtime variable values block by block (LDB) beats having the model explain or imagine the run: HumanEval GPT-3.5 seed 73.8 to 82.9 vs Self-Debug 81.1; GPT-4 seed 87.2 to 89.6 vs 88.4; Reflexion seed 91.5 to 95.1 vs 92.1. Gaps are small at strong seeds. Re-checked.
agent_test: Test tracing locals vs prose reasoning on logic bugs at equal tokens.

claim: At equal compute, self-repair does not clearly beat drawing more independent samples; the bottleneck is the model's own diagnosis. GPT-4 pass-rate ratio: 10 samples + 1 repair 1.05, 2 samples + 10 repairs 0.97 (GPT-3.5 cells mostly below 1). Human feedback raises repair success from 33.30% to 52.60% (intro 42.64/62.21, interview 19.33/45.67, competition 3.67/14.67). Tables re-checked.
agent_test: Match total tokens between resample-N and diagnose-and-repair arms.

claim: Repair benefit depends on correct location and diagnosis: in agent pipelines the correct-edit-location rate tracks solve rate, but file-level location alone is not enough (StarShip 23.67% resolved; paper text says 90.0% file-level, its table says 79.0%). Update (gap search): with strong 2026 bash-only agents, predicted locations changed pass@1 by -4.45 to +0.40 points (none significant), so the benefit shrinks as agents get better at finding files themselves.
agent_test: Measure location accuracy and resolve rate per arm; check the correlation holds inside our agent.

claim: Hierarchical localisation (file, then function, then line) in a fixed pipeline matched or beat open agents: Agentless 32.00% (96/300) at $0.70 on SWE-bench Lite. Re-checked. SWE-bench Lite has 4.3% exact-patch-in-issue, 10.0% missing-information and 5.0% misleading problems.
agent_test: Compare coarse-to-fine location steps against free exploration at equal tokens.

claim: Failed agent runs usually find the right file (72-81% of failed trajectories); failure is mostly in the fix or in symbol-level localisation, so file-level location is not the bottleneck on SWE-bench. Update: a 16,758-trajectory study puts the right-location-wrong-patch share at 60.8% to 69.1% for capable models (GPT-5, Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3-235B), but only 37.6% to 45.5% for small Qwen3 models.
agent_test: Log where failures occur (file, symbol, patch) for our agent.

claim: Debugging effectiveness of LLMs decays roughly exponentially over retries: most models lose 60-80% within 2-3 attempts, and a fresh start raises accuracy (llama3.1:8b 72.56 to 82.82; deepseek-coder-v2:16b 84.1 to 92.1). Re-checked. Small open models only. Update: full text shows HumanEval only, 18 mostly small models; fresh-start gains up to +9.8 points for weak models, about zero or slightly negative for strong ones; no frontier or repo-level test; token-neutral claim unsupported.
agent_test: Compare keep-revising vs restart-with-summary after 2 failed rounds at equal tokens.

claim: Runtime feedback helps syntax and reference bugs but is unhelpful or harmful for logic bugs (DebugBench, GPT-4 and GPT-3.5); figure values not extracted.
agent_test: Split our debug set by bug type before judging a feedback step.

claim: Interactive debugger access helps strong models and may hurt weak ones when given from the start; adding it after 5 failed rewrites helped every model per the text (Claude 3.7 Sonnet SWE-bench Lite rewrite 37.2, debug 48.4, debug(5) 52.1, confirmed). The extracted table for weak models (GPT-4o 17.2 to 23.6) does not match the text. Update (gap search): tables re-read. SWE-bench Lite: pdb from start hurts GPT-4o (19.1 to 17.2) and GPT-4o-mini (4.0 to 3.5), helps o1-preview (10.7 to 30.2), Claude 3.7 (37.2 to 48.4); pdb after 5 failures beats rewrite for all 6 models. Text-versus-table conflict is limited to Llama-3.3-70B (2.4 to 4.0). Real debugger beat simulated one by 8.0 and 4.6 points in InspectCoder.
agent_test: Gate the debugger tool until after first failed attempt; compare with tool-from-start.

claim: Human hypotheses early in debugging are mostly wrong (initial guesses wrong almost 90% of the time, cited; stage-two control hypotheses 3 of 27 correct), and tools that give potential hypotheses raise success (odds ratio 6.24) while fault-location lists do not (OR 1.4, p=0.64). Alaboudi not re-opened.
agent_test: Offer the agent a list of candidate causes vs a list of locations; measure fix rate.

claim: Ranked fault-localisation lists are contested for humans: Parnin and Orso 2011 found no overall speed gain (N=24), Xia et al. 2016 with 36 professionals found large gains (11.38 vs 26.45 min). Unresolved (tool accuracy, participants, bugs differ); sources not re-opened.
agent_test: Test with a rank-ordered suspect list of varying accuracy; check whether the agent reads it in order.

claim: Vessey's expert/novice contrast: experts commit less to early hypotheses, keep a system view and examine more modules; novices re-read the faulty module more. Founding result rests on N=16, one COBOL program, an ex post expert label, and no replication was found. Update: no modern replication or eye-tracking test of Vessey found; naturalistic data (11 professionals, 89 episodes) show no clean phase order.
schema_part: S4/G (do not anchor on first hypothesis)
agent_test: Hold two hypotheses open before the first edit; compare with commit-early at equal tokens.

claim: Looking at output first, reading in order vs mentally executing, and a familiarity phase did not separate experts from novices in Vessey 1985.
agent_test: No test; low priority.

claim: Execution-grounded multi-role debuggers (probe, analyse trace, repair with rollback) outperform plain repair loops; removing the repair loop drops 89.04 to 53.77. Preprint, own benchmarks.
agent_test: Add a keep-only-if-strictly-better rule to revise.

claim: Explanations of why a patch is right improve human review accuracy in 5 of 6 bugs but not review time, and made 2 cases worse.
agent_test: Not a priority.

claim: Debugging in practice is frequent and uneven and mostly not done with debugger tools: debugger unused in 91% of IDE sessions, debugging 13.7% of IDE time, reading precedes 51.9% of debug intervals.
agent_test: Descriptive only.

claim: In 2026 agentic repair with strong models, giving a predicted fault location does not raise pass@1 on average (17 of 18 settings slightly negative, -4.45 to +0.40 points, none significant after correction) and often raises end-to-end tokens. Gold locations help (+0.8 to +4.0 for files), gold bug causes help more (+4.4 to +7.0).
agent_test: Make location optional: run it when the task names few location clues; always keep the cause statement.

claim: When supplied locations are mostly wrong, repair collapses: with a spectrum tool the right function was in the top 3 for 28 of 100 Java faults and pass@1 fell from 15-19% to 0.3-3.6% across 5 models. Misleading locations anchor agents (34.5% to 100%) but about half still reach the gold file later.
agent_test: Verify a self-made location with one cheap execution check before editing; no break-even accuracy has been measured.

claim: Predicted file-level localization raises SWE-bench Verified resolve rate by about 4 points (44.7% to 48.9-49.1%), gold by 7.7 (52.4%); better reasoned localization lifted Agentless from 51.6% to 58.2%. Gains hold for pipeline agents with weaker repair models, in contrast to K20.
agent_test: Locate-first helps pipelines and weaker backbones more than strong bash agents.

claim: A cause-level step helps more than a location step: removing the suggestion stage cost 13.3 points (51.3% to 38.0%) at nearly equal localization accuracy; for humans, candidate causes gave OR 6.24 vs 1.4 for locations. No LLM study tested cause lists against location lists head to head.
agent_test: State the suspected cause in one sentence before editing.

claim: Failures on SWE-bench Verified are mostly after reaching the right code: 60.8% to 69.1% of failed runs for capable models. Agents also overwrite correct intermediate patches (5 bit-identical-to-gold patches lost).
agent_test: Keep a best-so-far patch and revert to it when later edits do not improve the checks.

claim: Real tracing beats model-simulated tracing for logic bugs: InspectCoder 67.87% vs 58.86% without a real debugger on BigCodeBench-R and 12.58% vs 7.95% on LiveCodeBench-R (Qwen2.5-Max); print debugging beat rubber-duck by 17.9% on medium LeetCode with GPT-4. Not tested against frontier models or equal-token resampling.
agent_test: Prefer executing and printing over narrating the run.

claim: Gaps still open after this pass: matched-token self-repair vs resampling for 2025-2026 reasoning models (K06), Parnin and Orso vs Xia 2016 (K14), expert-hypothesis replication of Vessey (K15), and whether a reproduction rerun cuts false-positive fixes.
agent_test: Treat as unknown; do not build rules on them.
